# Overview

The MCF7-SIX1 counterpart to `01_`: the same six panels, the same NanoLuc
constructs, against the MCF7-SIX1 expressed transcriptome and the mRNAs eIF3d
promotes in MCF7-SIX1 hypoxia (1hr, `te_lfc > 0.5`, `te_padj < 0.05`).

The reporter sequences are cell-line independent, so all of that machinery is
shared with `01_` via `reporter_helpers.R`. Four things differ, and each is a
place a careless copy of `01_` would go wrong:

1. **Directionality is opposite.** The MCF7-SIX1 DESeq2 interaction coefficient is
   log2(KD / sictrl), so a positive value means eIF3d *inhibits*. The 231 files
   carry the opposite orientation. This notebook reads the already-negated,
   promotes-positive tables written by
   `code/translational_control_overview/10m_mcf7six1_outcome_prep.Rmd` rather than
   negating again, so the sign is applied exactly once in the repo.
2. **The usual direction check does not apply.** The standing check is "the
   knockdown target's own `rna_lfc` must be strongly positive", but the MCF7-SIX1
   source has no `rna_lfc` column, so that check would *skip* rather than fail and
   the run would proceed unverified. Section 2 uses the rulers that do work here.
3. **Its own transcriptome and its own isoforms.** The background is
   `feature_matrix_tco_mcf7six1.rds`, built with MCF7-SIX1 dominant-transcript
   selection. 34.8% of shared genes pick a different dominant transcript than in
   231, so the 231 matrix would assign many genes the wrong isoform's features.
4. **Only one timepoint exists.** MCF7-SIX1 has 1hr only; there is no 4hr, 24hr or
   time-regressed counterpart.

Set sizes are not comparable to `01_` and should not be read as a cell-line
difference in effect size: 231 is spike-in normalized and MCF7-SIX1 is not.

All CDS metrics, genes and reporters alike, are computed on **stop-codon-free
ORFs**, and the junction + PEST tail counts as part of the reporter CDS because it
is part of what was cloned.

# Load Libraries

```{r load_libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(GenomicFeatures)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
library(Biostrings)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))
```

```{r params}
lfc_cutoff  <- 0.5
padj_cutoff <- 0.05
show_nanoluc_core <- FALSE

cat("lfc_cutoff =", lfc_cutoff, "| padj_cutoff =", padj_cutoff,
    "| show_nanoluc_core =", show_nanoluc_core, "\n")
```

# 1. NanoLuc Construct: Import and Verify

Identical to `01_`: the construct is cell-line independent.

```{r read_nanoluc}
nl <- load_nanoluc_construct()
```

```{r nanoluc_table}
nl_df <- tibble(
  reporter   = c("NanoLuc construct", "NanoLuc ORF only", "Junction + PEST tag"),
  cds_length = c(nchar(nl$full), nchar(nl$core), nchar(nl$pest)),
  gc_pct     = c(orf_gc_pct(nl$full), gc_pct_of(nl$core), gc_pct_of(nl$pest)),
  gc3_pct    = c(orf_gc3_pct(nl$full), compute_gc3_pct(nl$core),
                 compute_gc3_pct(nl$pest))
)

stopifnot(
  "Reporter GC% out of range"  = all(nl_df$gc_pct  >= 0 & nl_df$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "Reporter GC3% out of range" = all(nl_df$gc3_pct >= 0 & nl_df$gc3_pct <= 100)
)

print(nl_df %>% mutate(across(c(gc_pct, gc3_pct), ~ round(.x, 1))))

luc_df <- nl_df %>%
  filter(reporter %in% c("NanoLuc construct",
                         if (show_nanoluc_core) "NanoLuc ORF only")) %>%
  mutate(color = c("#0072B2", "#CC79A7")[seq_len(n())],
         linetype = "solid")

cat("Reference lines drawn:", paste(luc_df$reporter, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# 2. MCF7-SIX1 Gene Set and the Direction Check

```{r load_mcf7_te}
te_path <- here("output",
                "translation_categories_si3d_vs_sictrl_mcf7six1_hypoxia_1hr.csv")
stopifnot(
  "MCF7-SIX1 promotes-positive table not found; knit 10m_mcf7six1_outcome_prep.Rmd first" =
    file.exists(te_path))

te_mcf <- read_csv(te_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot("Expected the promotes-positive column layout from 10m_" =
            all(c("gene_id", "symbol", "te_lfc", "te_padj",
                  "source_log2FoldChange") %in% names(te_mcf)))
cat("MCF7-SIX1 si3d hypoxia 1hr table:", nrow(te_mcf), "genes\n")
```

The 231 direction check cannot run here, so three rulers replace it. All three are
assertions, not prints, and none of them can pass by skipping.

```{r direction_check}
# Ruler A: the table on disk really is the negation of the source. Both columns
# are present, so this is a check that can fail rather than one that skips.
stopifnot("te_lfc is not the negation of source_log2FoldChange" =
            max(abs(te_mcf$te_lfc + te_mcf$source_log2FoldChange),
                na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-8)
cat("Ruler A - te_lfc == -source_log2FoldChange for all",
    sum(!is.na(te_mcf$te_lfc)), "genes\n")

# Ruler B: the depleted factor's own TE. In the raw MCF7-SIX1 orientation
# log2(KD/sictrl), EIF3D is strongly POSITIVE (~+1.79). Promotes-positive is the
# negation, so EIF3D must be strongly NEGATIVE here - the same orientation 231's
# EIF3D te_lfc has (-1.26). A flipped sign would put EIF3D in the promoted set.
eif3d <- te_mcf %>% filter(symbol == "EIF3D")
stopifnot(
  "EIF3D not found in the MCF7-SIX1 table" = nrow(eif3d) == 1,
  "EIF3D te_lfc is not strongly negative: the negation may have been lost" =
    eif3d$te_lfc < -1,
  "EIF3D raw log2FoldChange is not strongly positive in the source" =
    eif3d$source_log2FoldChange > 1
)
cat("Ruler B - EIF3D te_lfc:", round(eif3d$te_lfc, 2),
    "(source", round(eif3d$source_log2FoldChange, 2),
    "); strongly negative in promotes-positive orientation, as expected\n")

# Ruler C: the derived set must reproduce the gene set 42_ already wrote. This
# ties the cutoffs applied here to the committed set rather than re-deriving a
# near-miss of it.
promotes <- te_mcf %>%
  filter(te_lfc > lfc_cutoff, te_padj < padj_cutoff) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))

gs_path <- here("output", "genesets",
                "mcf7six1_hypoxia_3d_promotes_TE_1hr_lfc0.5.csv")
stopifnot("MCF7-SIX1 geneset CSV not found" = file.exists(gs_path))
gs <- read_csv(gs_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

stopifnot("Derived promoted set does not reproduce the committed geneset CSV" =
            setequal(promotes$gene_id_clean, gs$ensembl_gene))
cat("Ruler C - derived set reproduces", nrow(gs),
    "committed geneset genes exactly\n")

# EIF3D must not be in its own promoted set, which it would be under a flip.
stopifnot("EIF3D is in the promoted set: direction is flipped" =
            !"EIF3D" %in% promotes$symbol)

cat("\nMCF7-SIX1 eIF3d hypoxia-promoted genes (te_lfc >", lfc_cutoff,
    ", te_padj <", padj_cutoff, "):", nrow(promotes), "\n")
cat("Median te_lfc across the table:", round(median(te_mcf$te_lfc, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    "(MCF7-SIX1 is not spike-in normalized; 231 medians are shifted positive)\n")
```

# 3. Transcript Selection: MCF7-SIX1 Own Isoforms

```{r load_feature_matrix}
fm_path <- here("output", "translational_control_overview",
                "feature_matrix_tco_mcf7six1.rds")
stopifnot("MCF7-SIX1 feature matrix not found" = file.exists(fm_path))

fm <- readRDS(fm_path)
stopifnot("MCF7-SIX1 matrix is missing the standard id columns" =
            all(c("transcript_id_clean", "gene_id_clean", "symbol") %in% names(fm)))

tx_all <- fm %>% dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)

# This matrix is one dominant transcript per gene; if that ever stops holding,
# the "expressed transcriptome" curve would double-count genes.
stopifnot("MCF7-SIX1 matrix is not one transcript per gene" =
            n_distinct(tx_all$gene_id_clean) == nrow(tx_all))

tx_promotes <- tx_all %>% filter(gene_id_clean %in% promotes$gene_id_clean)

n_missing <- nrow(promotes) - nrow(tx_promotes)
cat("All expressed genes in MCF7-SIX1 matrix:", nrow(tx_all), "\n")
cat("Promoted genes found in matrix:", nrow(tx_promotes), "of", nrow(promotes),
    paste0("(", n_missing, " not in the matrix, excluded)\n"))

# No salmon fallback here, unlike 01_. The MCF7-SIX1 quant files live in the
# other repo and cover siCTRL NORMOXIA only, so they cannot supply a hypoxia
# dominant isoform. The excluded genes are reported rather than filled in with
# an isoform chosen under the wrong condition.
stopifnot("More than 10% of promoted genes are missing from the matrix" =
            n_missing / nrow(promotes) < 0.10)
```

# 4. CDS Sequences, Lengths, GC and GC3

```{r build_metrics}
metrics_all <- build_cds_metrics(
  here("accessories", "human", "txdb.gencode49.sqlite"))

expressed <- tx_all %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>%
  filter(cds_length > 0)

promoted <- tx_promotes %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>%
  filter(cds_length > 0)

cat("Expressed transcriptome - valid CDS:", nrow(expressed), "of", nrow(tx_all), "\n")
cat("eIF3d promoted        - valid CDS:", nrow(promoted), "of", nrow(tx_promotes), "\n")

stopifnot(
  "GC% out of range"  = all(expressed$gc_pct  >= 0 & expressed$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "GC3% out of range" = all(expressed$gc3_pct >= 0 & expressed$gc3_pct <= 100),
  "GC3 median not in expected range [40, 65]" =
    between(median(expressed$gc3_pct), 40, 65),
  "Promoted set is empty after the CDS join" = nrow(promoted) > 0
)

# Biological spot-check: ACTB CDS GC% expected 50-70%.
actb <- expressed %>% filter(symbol == "ACTB") %>% dplyr::slice(1)
if (nrow(actb) == 1) {
  stopifnot("ACTB CDS GC% outside expected 50-70%" = between(actb$gc_pct, 50, 70))
  cat("ACTB CDS GC%:", round(actb$gc_pct, 2),
      "| GC3%:", round(actb$gc3_pct, 2), "\n")
}
```

# 5. Density Panels with the NanoLuc Reference Line

The grey curve is the whole expressed MCF7-SIX1 transcriptome, including the
promoted genes. The Wilcoxon test is run against the transcriptome **excluding**
the promoted set, so the two samples are disjoint, and is reported to the console
rather than annotated on the panel.

```{r density_setup}
group_cols <- c("All expressed mRNAs"    = "grey70",
                "eIF3d hypoxia promotes" = "#E69F00")
```

```{r panel_length, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_len <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "cds_length",
  xlab    = "CDS length (kb)",
  title   = "CDS length, MCF7-SIX1",
  outfile = "cds_reporter_02_density_cds_length_mcf7six1.pdf",
  luc_tbl = luc_df, group_cols = group_cols,
  xscale  = 1000, xmax = 6
)
```

```{r panel_gc, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_gc <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "gc_pct",
  xlab    = "CDS GC content (%)",
  title   = "CDS GC content, MCF7-SIX1",
  outfile = "cds_reporter_02_density_cds_gc_mcf7six1.pdf",
  luc_tbl = luc_df, group_cols = group_cols
)
```

```{r panel_gc3, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_gc3 <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "gc3_pct",
  xlab    = "CDS GC3 content (%)",
  title   = "CDS GC3 content, MCF7-SIX1",
  outfile = "cds_reporter_02_density_cds_gc3_mcf7six1.pdf",
  luc_tbl = luc_df, group_cols = group_cols
)
```

# 6. Designed NanoLuc Variants

The same four constructs as `01_`. They were designed against the **231** codon
preference, not MCF7-SIX1, so these panels ask where a 231-designed reporter lands
in MCF7-SIX1 rather than showing a MCF7-SIX1-specific design. A MCF7-SIX1 design
would need its own bg-RSCU pass.

```{r load_designed_variants}
var_df <- load_nanoluc_variants(nl)

cat("\nORF as designed vs construct as cloned:\n")
print(var_df %>%
        dplyr::select(reporter, n_codons_changed,
                      orf_length, gc3_orf, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct) %>%
        mutate(across(c(gc3_orf, gc_pct, gc3_pct), ~ round(.x, 1))))

gc3_collision <-
  var_df$gc3_pct[var_df$reporter == "3d-negative control"] ==
  var_df$gc3_pct[var_df$reporter == "NanoLuc parent"]
cat("Negative control GC3 identical to parent:", gc3_collision,
    "(drawn dashed so both remain visible)\n")

var_plot_df <- var_df %>%
  dplyr::select(reporter, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct) %>%
  mutate(
    color    = c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "black"),
    linetype = c("solid",   "solid",   "solid",   "22")
  )
```

```{r panel_variants_length, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_len_var <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "cds_length",
  xlab    = "CDS length (kb)",
  title   = "CDS length, MCF7-SIX1, NanoLuc constructs",
  outfile = "cds_reporter_02_density_cds_length_variants_mcf7six1.pdf",
  luc_tbl = var_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols,
  xscale  = 1000, xmax = 6
)
```

```{r panel_variants_gc, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_gc_var <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "gc_pct",
  xlab    = "CDS GC content (%)",
  title   = "CDS GC content, MCF7-SIX1, NanoLuc constructs",
  outfile = "cds_reporter_02_density_cds_gc_variants_mcf7six1.pdf",
  luc_tbl = var_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols
)
```

```{r panel_variants_gc3, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_gc3_var <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "gc3_pct",
  xlab    = "CDS GC3 content (%)",
  title   = "CDS GC3 content, MCF7-SIX1, NanoLuc constructs",
  outfile = "cds_reporter_02_density_cds_gc3_variants_mcf7six1.pdf",
  luc_tbl = var_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols
)
```

# 7. Where NanoLuc Falls: Percentiles

```{r percentiles}
ref_all <- bind_rows(
  luc_df      %>% dplyr::select(reporter, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct),
  var_plot_df %>% dplyr::select(reporter, cds_length, gc_pct, gc3_pct)
)

pct_tbl <- reporter_percentiles(expressed, promoted, ref_all)
print(pct_tbl)

stopifnot("Percentiles must lie in [0, 100]" =
            all(pct_tbl$pct_expressed >= 0 & pct_tbl$pct_expressed <= 100 &
                pct_tbl$pct_promoted  >= 0 & pct_tbl$pct_promoted  <= 100))

write_csv(pct_tbl,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
               "02_nanoluc_percentiles_vs_mcf7six1.csv"))
cat("Exported: output/cds_reporter_design/02_nanoluc_percentiles_vs_mcf7six1.csv\n")
```

```{r group_medians}
medians_df <- tibble(
  group = c("All expressed mRNAs", "eIF3d hypoxia promotes"),
  n     = c(nrow(expressed), nrow(promoted)),
  median_len_kb  = c(median(expressed$cds_length), median(promoted$cds_length)) / 1000,
  median_gc_pct  = c(median(expressed$gc_pct),  median(promoted$gc_pct)),
  median_gc3_pct = c(median(expressed$gc3_pct), median(promoted$gc3_pct))
) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("median"), ~ round(.x, 2)))

print(medians_df)

write_csv(medians_df,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
               "02_group_medians_cds_gc_mcf7six1.csv"))
cat("Exported: output/cds_reporter_design/02_group_medians_cds_gc_mcf7six1.csv\n")
```

# 8. Side by Side with MDA-MB-231

`01_` must have been knit first. This reads its exported medians rather than
recomputing them, so the two cell lines cannot drift apart.

```{r compare_231, eval = file.exists(here("output", "cds_reporter_design", "01_group_medians_cds_gc.csv"))}
m231 <- read_csv(here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
                      "01_group_medians_cds_gc.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

cmp <- bind_rows(
  m231      %>% mutate(cell_line = "MDA-MB-231"),
  medians_df %>% mutate(cell_line = "MCF7-SIX1")
) %>%
  dplyr::select(cell_line, group, n, median_len_kb, median_gc_pct, median_gc3_pct) %>%
  arrange(group, cell_line)

print(cmp)

write_csv(cmp, here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
                    "02_group_medians_both_celllines.csv"))
cat("Exported: output/cds_reporter_design/02_group_medians_both_celllines.csv\n")

# The two promoted sets are defined on differently normalized data and differ in
# size by several fold, so these medians describe each cell line's own landscape
# and are not a like-for-like effect-size comparison.
cat("\nSet sizes differ partly because 231 is spike-in normalized and",
    "MCF7-SIX1 is not; read each cell line's panels on their own terms.\n")
```

# 9. Summary

```{r summary}
cat("=== CDS reporter design: NanoLuc vs MCF7-SIX1 ===\n\n")

cat("NanoLuc construct (stop-free):", nchar(nl$full), "nt |",
    nchar(nl$full) / 3, "codons\n")
cat("  GC%  =", round(gc_pct_of(nl$full), 1),
    "| GC3% =", round(compute_gc3_pct(nl$full), 1), "\n\n")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(medians_df))) {
  cat(sprintf("%-24s n = %-6s  median length %.2f kb | GC %.1f%% | GC3 %.1f%%\n",
              medians_df$group[i], fmt_n(medians_df$n[i]),
              medians_df$median_len_kb[i], medians_df$median_gc_pct[i],
              medians_df$median_gc3_pct[i]))
}
cat("\n")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(pct_tbl))) {
  cat(sprintf("%-20s %-11s %8.1f  ->  %5.1f pct of expressed, %5.1f pct of promoted\n",
              pct_tbl$reporter[i], pct_tbl$metric[i], pct_tbl$reporter_value[i],
              pct_tbl$pct_expressed[i], pct_tbl$pct_promoted[i]))
}
```
